chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Does the fasting person [have any issue if he] smells rosemary and perfume?' He said: 'There is no harm.'
ai.seo_question: Does smelling perfume or rosemary break the fast in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the mere act of inhaling pleasant scents like rosemary or perfume does not break the fast, distinguishing it from substances that are swallowed. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for validating daily activities involving aromatherapy or natural scents during Ramadan, provided no part of the scent is ingested. It reflects the juristic principle that the fast is invalidated by consumption or entry of matter into the body cavities, not by sensory perception alone.
